gap: No result ChatGPT got states that in CNC Kitchen's same-model test, a 4-colour cube took 7 hours on the Bambu Lab H2C in Purge Saving mode. The two full toolchangers, the Snapmaker U1 and the Prusa XL, each printed it in under 4 hours. The H2C took about 40 s per colour change including purge, against 10–15 s on a toolchanger.
standout_why: I compared against 3dtoolchangers.com/printers (cited), 3dprinteray.com/toolchanger-printers (cited, verified 2026-10-14) and tomshardware.com/best-picks/best-3d-printers (cited). The first two give only maker or retailer specs and prices: tool counts, build volume, chamber temperature, and Snapmaker's '~5 s' and Prusa's '~12 s' claims. Neither has a single figure measured by a named tester, and 3dtoolchangers says its own lab has 'no published runs.' The Tom's Hardware best-picks page only returned its title, so I can't rule out that it holds some of these numbers. Tom's Hardware also has separate H2C, U1 and INDX reviews with measured grams, which I could not open (see unsourced). That uncertainty is why this scores 2, not 3.
decides: This backs the full-toolchanger pick over the H2C, which ChatGPT listed 'from around $2,199' as an alternative. One reviewer, on the same model, measured the $749 Snapmaker U1 and the Prusa XL at about twice the H2C's multicolour speed. Notebookcheck adds a caution for the Creator 5 Pro: it needed 28 minutes of preparation before a 4-filament print, and its factory settings made 36 g of waste on a 16 g Benchy until the reviewer tuned it down to 8 g. On waste, CNC Kitchen found the U1's prime tower 'a bit' larger than the XL's, so the U1's edge is price and speed, not the lowest waste.

findings.label: Print time, 4-colour test cube (Purge Saving mode)
findings.source_title: The H2C Review: Better Than a Toolchanger? (CNC Kitchen, Stefan Hermann, 2025-11-18)
findings.note: Quote: 'took 7 hours to print on the H2C in Purge Saving mode.' The review says standard purge mode is 'about 10% slower', so roughly 7.7 h by my arithmetic. Same model printed on the U1, Prusa XL, H2D and P2S.

findings.label: Print time, same 4-colour test cube
findings.source_title: The H2C Review: Better Than a Toolchanger? (CNC Kitchen, Stefan Hermann, 2025-11-18)
findings.note: Quote: 'Both toolchangers were around twice as fast and printed the cube in less than 4 hours.' The two toolchangers are the Prusa XL and the Snapmaker U1. Overall the review puts the H2C 'around 50–100% slower than on a toolchanger.'

findings.label: Print time, same 4-colour test cube
findings.source_title: The H2C Review: Better Than a Toolchanger? (CNC Kitchen, Stefan Hermann, 2025-11-18)
findings.note: Same sentence as the U1 row. The test machine was the XL with toolchanger, not necessarily the current XL+ revision.

findings.label: Colour change time including purge
findings.value: about 40 s (vs 10–15 s on a toolchanger)
findings.source_title: The H2C Review: Better Than a Toolchanger? (CNC Kitchen, Stefan Hermann, 2025-11-18)
findings.note: Quote: 'Including purging, this takes around 40 seconds compared to 10–15 seconds on a toolchanger.' The mechanical nozzle swap alone 'doesn't even take 15 seconds'. About 20 s is AMS idle time and about 10 s is tower purge. The review gives 1–2 min for single-nozzle AMS machines.

findings.label: Waste, 4-colour test cube (28 g model)
findings.value: 23 g prime tower (Purge Saving mode); about 50% heavier in normal mode
findings.source_title: The H2C Review: Better Than a Toolchanger? (CNC Kitchen, Stefan Hermann, 2025-11-18)
findings.note: Quote: 'the prime tower, which weighs 23 g compared to the 28 g of the model itself.' On the same model the review says the H2D 'purges and flushes eight times more material', and the P2S made 'over 320 g of poops and purge tower.'

findings.label: Waste vs Prusa XL, same test cube
findings.value: Prime towers 'more or less comparable', with the U1 'wasting a bit more'
findings.source_title: The H2C Review: Better Than a Toolchanger? (CNC Kitchen, Stefan Hermann, 2025-11-18)
findings.note: No gram figure is given for the U1 or XL towers. The review says both toolchangers 'are even faster and produce less waste' than the H2C for multicolour PLA.

findings.label: Preparation time before a 4-filament print
findings.value: 28 min (about 10 min on later prints with the same bed and material)
findings.source_title: Four print heads, less waste: Creator 5 Pro tested (Notebookcheck, Silvio Werner, published 2026-08-10, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Quote: 'For a print using all four filaments, we measured a preparation time of 28 minutes.'

findings.label: Waste, 4-colour Benchy (16 g model)
findings.value: 36 g on factory settings; 8 g after tuning
findings.source_title: Four print heads, less waste: Creator 5 Pro tested (Notebookcheck, Silvio Werner, published 2026-08-10, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Quote: 'the factory settings produced a hefty 36 grams of waste for a model weighing just 16 grams'. Optimisation brought it 'first to 15 grams and then to just 8 grams.' The print had more than 700 tool changes.

findings.label: Print time, 4-colour Benchy (tuned)
findings.source_title: Four print heads, less waste: Creator 5 Pro tested (Notebookcheck, Silvio Werner, published 2026-08-10, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Measured with optimised settings. Notebookcheck sets this against Bambu Studio's estimate of 'more than 18 hours' on a single-nozzle printer, which is a slicer estimate, not a measurement.

unsourced: Tom's Hardware Prusa CORE One+ INDX review (tomshardware.com/3d-printing/prusa-core-one-plus-indx-review, Denise Bertacchi, reportedly 2026-09-20): it reportedly measured 18 g of waste over 1,646 tool changes, a run nearly 9 h faster than the H2C, and 83.58 g less waste than the H2C on the same model. WebFetch returned only the page title. I saw the figures only in search snippets and a SimplyPrint summary page (simplyprint.io/compatibility/prusa-core-one-plus-indx.md), so I left them out.

Tom's Hardware Snapmaker U1 review (tomshardware.com/3d-printing/snapmaker-u1-review): search snippets show a boat print of 1 h 19 min with 7 g of prime tower, and 0.76 g on a 22 min 45 s print, on a beta unit. The page returned only its title, and the 3dtested.com mirror returned HTTP 525.
Tom's Hardware Bambu Lab H2C review: the page and its 3dtested.com mirror both failed to load (title only, then HTTP 525).
TechRadar Prusa CORE One+ INDX 8-Tool review (Alastair Jennings, tested against the H2C and U1): the page returned only its title, so I have no numbers.
A measured, independent tool-change time in seconds for the Snapmaker U1, Creator 5 Pro or CORE One+ INDX. I found only the maker claims (U1 about 5 s, Flashforge 7 s, Prusa about 12 s).
Measured noise (dB) or power draw for any of the candidates. Notebookcheck reports neither for the Creator 5 Pro.
Measured figures for the current Prusa XL+ revision specifically. CNC Kitchen's test machine was the Prusa XL toolchanger.
